Nielsen Marketing Cloud Services Privacy Notice (UK)

Updated: December 2025

Nielsen Marketing Cloud ("NMC") is a product or service offered by Nielsen Media Research Limited ("NMRL", "we" or "us"). NMRL has a registered office at Endeavour House, 189 Shaftesbury Avenue, London, WC2H 8JR, United Kingdom and is the data controller for the personal data processed as described in this Privacy Notice.

NMRL is committed to protecting the privacy of data subjects and processing personal data in an open and transparent manner. This Privacy Notice describes both the way in which we collect and process personal data in connection with our services and the legal bases on which we rely for such processing in accordance with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR). For the purposes of this Privacy Notice, "personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ("data subject", or "you"). This Privacy Notice also outlines data subjects" choices and legal rights in relation to their personal data.

Depending on the services provided to clients, NMRL may act as a data controller or a data processor. Further information regarding roles under the UK GDPR is provided in the Legal Bases section below.

Joint Controllers

NMRL sometimes acts jointly with other Nielsen companies when making decisions about your personal data. Specifically, joint decisions are made when two or more Nielsen companies share personal data with each other, for example, when providing services to a global client. NMRL, however, remains responsible for obligations under the UK GDPR as regards the rights of data subjects which are outlined in the "Your legal rights" section below. For more information on NMRL Joint Controllers please see the "How personal data is shared" section below.

This Privacy Notice only applies to personal data that is processed by NMRL for the provision of its NMC services. Any personal data obtained by NMRL from third parties for its NMC product is governed by their own privacy notices. As the services offered by these third parties are not owned and controlled by NMRL, we encourage you to review the privacy notices of each platform, website, and mobile application ("mobile app") that you access or use to learn how third parties may use their data.


A. Sources of personal data

NMC obtains data from the following sources:

  • Online advertiser and publisher websites and web applications. We use our technology on websites owned by companies with advertising space to gather data about a user's visit to a website (e.g., number of visits, average time spent, pages viewed, navigation history through the website, and other statistics);
  • Mobile App Developers/Owners who provide us with data from mobile apps;
  • Third Party Data Providers who may not have a direct relationship with you but combine data from multiple sources (e.g. publishers and websites) and share it with their clients for purposes of data analytics that support behavioural and targeted online advertising; and
  • when you participate in an online quiz hosted by VisualDNA, a product offered by NMRL.

This data is sorted into categories based on demographics, interests, and preferences and made available to our Clients. Our Clients use the data we provide to carry out interest-based advertising and to provide a more relevant advertising experience to consumers.

B. Types of personal data collected

Desktop: IP address, cookie ID, browser type, language, access times, pages visited, and referring website addresses.

Mobile Device: IP address, Cookie ID, device type and model, mobile browser, operating system, carrier name and identifiers assigned to your device, such as an Apple IDFA and Google Advertising ID.

We also collect the approximate geographic area (i.e. country, city, town, district) derived from your IP address or geolocation information of your mobile device if location services have been enabled.

C. Methods of data collection

We collect information about your computer and/or mobile device online activity via the technologies described below:

  • cookies. Cookies are small text files that are stored on a user's browser and can be accessed by web servers when the browser returns to a website or goes to another website. We use cookies to gather data about a user's visit to a website (e.g., number of visits, average time spent, pages viewed, navigation history through the website, and other statistics);
  • HTML tags. HTML tags are small strings of code that are used to generate the cookie described above; and
  • server-to-server connection. We obtain data, such as an IP address, email address or unique device ID, that relates to users' browsers and/or mobile devices, from other online and offline third-party sources directly through connections to their servers and other secure data transfer methods.
D. How we use personal data

In this section we outline the purposes for which we process personal data for the provision of our services to our Clients.

We use data obtained from the different sources described above to build profiles for advertising purposes. More specifically, we provide insights to our clients by grouping this data into various categories based on demographics, interests, and/or preferences (e.g., women in the Paris region aged between 20 and 40 who are likely to be interested in fashion and certain clothing items). We do this by using data about your visits to different websites to make inferences about the types of ads and content that may be of interest to you.

We also process data to create segments (i.e., categories of users grouped by common traits or preferences such as lifestyle and leisure, entertainment, technology). These segments enable our clients to deliver more effective, relevant and specific advertising via web browsers and mobile apps to data subjects with matching profiles. Our Clients identify the categories of individuals to whom they wish to target specific ads, and we provide them with device or advertising identifiers that match those categories, which they or their partners (e.g., advertising agencies) can then use to deliver ads.

We also carry out cross device matching, which means we use data to make a deterministic or statistical match of mobile device advertising identifiers and cookie identifiers. For example, we or our partners may match a user's device if the user logs in to the same online service on multiple devices or web browsers or if the user's devices share similar attributes that support an inference that they belong to the same user. This allows a data subject to be associated with the same attributes across multiple devices. Our clients use this information to present relevant advertising across these devices. Neither NMC, nor our Clients have an intention to identify the data subject whose personal data is processed for this purpose.

We also process personal data for our internal business purposes, as outlined below:

  • Product Development: to develop new products and to improve our existing products and services.
  • Corporate transactions: In the event of a contemplated or actual reorganisation, merger, sale, joint venture, assignment, transfer or other disposition of all or any portion of our business or assets or stock, personal data may be used for the purposes of preparing and completing this transaction.
  • Legal obligations: We may use personal data where we are required to do so by law, for instance for the purposes of assessing and responding to legal and regulatory requests (including investigations, audits, accounting and financial matters), or where we consider it necessary to enforce, exercise or defend legal rights or claims.
  • Handling and responding to your requests: If a data subject asks us questions about our processing of their personal data or exercises any of their legal rights, we will use that data subject's personal data to assess and respond to such requests.

Because some of the personal data processed is collected indirectly (for example from a third party), NMRL provides specific information to meet the requirements of (UK) GDPR Article 14.5(b). This information is provided in its Article 14 Notice available here.

E. Legal bases for processing personal data

When we collect and process personal data via the use of our software on behalf of our Clients (i.e., where we are only permitted to process data collected on behalf of our Clients), we are typically acting as a data processor and rely on our Client's legal basis for processing the personal data on their behalf. To support the communication of data subject consent from our Clients for the delivery of relevant online advertising and content, NMRL participates as a vendor under the IAB Europe's Transparency & Consent Framework. For additional information about the Framework, please visit https://iabeurope.eu/ transparency-consent-framework/.

When we process personal data for our own purposes as a data controller (i.e. when we obtain data from third parties for our own use) we rely on one of the legal bases below in order to process such personal data.

  • Consent: This is the primary legal basis that we rely on for the processing of personal data for the delivery of our services. For example, we rely on the consent provided to our Clients and third party partners at the point of data collection or disclosure to us to process such personal data for all marketing and online advertising purposes, as outlined in the "How we use personal data" section. We require our third party partners to confirm that they have an appropriate legal basis for sharing that personal data with us. We also rely on the consent provided to our Clients and third party partners at the point of data collection or disclosure to us to process such personal data to improve our existing products and services or for new product development purposes.
  • Legitimate interests: We rely on our legitimate interests to process personal data for some purposes, provided that the processing remains compatible with the purpose for which your personal data was collected and that your interests, fundamental rights, or freedoms do not override such interests. In particular, we rely on our legitimate interests for the effective and lawful operation of our business, the prevention and detection of fraud, in the event of a corporate transaction, to save and communicate your privacy choices, and in order to handle and respond to data subject requests.
  • Compliance with legal obligations: We may process data subject's personal data if necessary for us to comply with a legal obligation arising under applicable law or to enforce, exercise or defend legal rights or claims.
F. How personal data is shared

We will share your personal data for different purposes, as described below:

  • With other Nielsen operated businesses, as a Joint Controller, to provide services to clients. The Joint Controllers and key processing activities involved are:
    • The Nielsen Company (US), LLC when working with global clients or third party data providers for services that include the UK market and involve the processing of personal data of UK data subjects as described in this privacy notice; in the event of a corporate transaction; where required to do so by law; and for security and fraud prevention.
    • eXelate Inc. (an affiliate of The Nielsen Company (US), LLC) when working with global clients or third party data providers for services that include the UK market and involve the processing of personal data of UK data subjects as described in this privacy notice ; in the event of a corporate transaction; where required to do so by law; and for security and fraud prevention.
    When our group companies make decisions jointly, those members of staff will ensure that each company involved complies with data protection rules.
  • With our Clients for the purposes referred to in this Privacy Notice. The sharing of personal data with our clients is a key part of how we provide our services to our Clients. For example, Nielsen Marketing Cloud cookie data allows Nielsen to let its advertising customers know whether consumers who clicked on an ad tend to fit into segments of inferred commercial interests, such as an interest in sports, gardening or cars. This helps Nielsen"s customers refine their advertising and other marketing-related communications. We also share data described in 'Types of personal data collected' with our Clients that match the categories of data subjects they wish to target specific ads to.
  • We share data with third parties that provide services to us, such as system hosting, management and support; data backup; and security and storage services. We exercise appropriate due diligence in the selection of third party service providers, and require that such providers maintain adequate technical and organisational security measures to safeguard personal data, and to process personal data only as instructed by us or a member of the group and for no other purposes.
  • We may share data if we have a legal obligation to do so or where we believe it is necessary to protect the rights, property, or safety of our business or any person.
  • In the event of a corporate transaction, such as a reorganisation, merger, sale, joint venture, assignment, transfer, or other disposition of all or any portion of our business, assets, or stock (including in connection with a bankruptcy or similar proceeding), all data collected or maintained by us may be shared with relevant third parties.
G. International transfers of personal data

The disclosures described in the "How personal data is shared" section above result in the transfer of your data to countries or regions with data protection laws that differ from those in your country of residence. We respect applicable local laws regarding cross-border transfers of and access to personal data and take steps to ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect such data.

The EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF), The UK Extension To The EU-U.S. DPF, and The SWISS-U.S. DPF

The Nielsen Company (US), LLC complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (EU-U.S. DPF), the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (Swiss-U.S. DPF) as set forth by the U.S. Department of Commerce. The Nielsen Company (US), LLC has certified to the U.S. Department of Commerce that it adheres to the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework Principles (EU-U.S. DPF Principles) with regard to the processing of personal data received from the European Union in reliance on the EU-U.S. DPF and from the United Kingdom (and Gibraltar) in reliance on the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF. The Nielsen Company (US), LLC has certified to the U.S. Department of Commerce that it adheres to the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework Principles (Swiss-U.S. DPF Principles) with regard to the processing of personal data received from Switzerland in reliance on the Swiss-U.S. DPF. If there is any conflict between the terms in this privacy policy and the EU-U.S. DPF Principles and/or the Swiss-U.S. DPF Principles, the Principles shall govern. To learn more about the Data Privacy Framework (DPF) program, and to view our certification, please visit https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/. The Federal Trade Commission has jurisdiction over The Nielsen Company (US), LLC"s compliance with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (EU-U.S. DPF) and the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (Swiss-U.S. DPF).

Internal Complaints Mechanism - (DPF)

In compliance with the EU-U.S. DPF and the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF and the Swiss-U.S. DPF, The Nielsen Company (US), LLC commits to resolve DPF Principles-related complaints about our collection and use of your personal information. EU and UK and Swiss individuals with inquiries or complaints regarding our handling of personal data received in reliance on the EU-U.S. DPF and the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF and the Swiss-U.S. DPF should first contact Nielsen"s Data Protection Officer at: privacy.department@nielsen.com.

Independent Recourse Mechanism - (DPF)

In compliance with the EU-U.S. DPF and the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF and the Swiss-U.S. DPF, The Nielsen Company (US), LLC commits to cooperate and comply respectively with the advice of the panel established by the EU data protection authorities (DPAs) and the UK Information Commissioner"s Office (ICO) and the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) and the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) with regard to unresolved complaints concerning our handling of personal data received in reliance on the EU-U.S. DPF and the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF and the Swiss-U.S. DPF.

In certain circumstances, the DPF provides the right to invoke binding arbitration to resolve complaints not resolved by other means, as described in Annex I to the DPF Principles.

Nielsen remains responsible for any of your personal information that is shared under the DPF Onward Transfer Principle with third parties for external processing on our behalf, as described in Section "F How personal data is shared".

To learn more about the DPF, and to view Nielsen's certification, please visit the DPF website.

H. Data security

We maintain physical, technical, and organisational security measures to protect personal data against accidental, unlawful, or unauthorised destruction, loss, alteration, disclosure, or access, wherever it is processed. We use generally-accepted industry security standards including physical, electronic, and administrative safeguards that are designed to help protect the data that we collect, use, and retain.

I. Children's data

Our products and services are not designed for or directed at children. We do not knowingly solicit, collect, or maintain personal data from children under the age of 18. Similarly, we prohibit third parties from whom we receive personal data from providing us with personal data from websites and mobile apps directed at children or from knowingly sharing with us data relating to children. If we become aware that we have collected or received personal data relating to a child, we will take reasonable steps to delete it.

J. Data Retention

We ensure that your personal data will not be stored longer than is necessary to fulfil our business purposes.

NMC stores cookies for a maximum duration of 120 days on websites where our cookie is present. However, we cease to use personal data collected from such a cookie 30 days after the last related device activity (e.g. if you do not visit the website where the cookie was placed). We retain aggregated pseudonymized cookie data to support the improvement of our products and services for up to 13 months.

As described in the "Data subject's Choices" section below, if you withdraw your consent for personal data processing, we will no longer process data associated with those identifiers. However, new data will be processed if you visit another website where our cookie is present using a different browser.

K. Data subject's choices

We are committed to providing you with choices with respect to how we process your personal data. This section describes how you can exercise these choices.

Web Browsers You can opt out of our data collection for interest-based advertising purposes at any time by clicking on our opt-out page. Please note that you should opt-out from every device and/or browser separately. After opting out, you will no longer be included in advertising and content targeting activities that are conducted by NMC. You will still receive online ads and content, but these ads and content may not be as personalised or relevant to you. We require our clients and third party partners to ensure opt out requests are communicated to us in a timely manner.

NMC is a member of several interest-based advertising self-regulatory groups, including the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance ("EDAA") and adheres to the self-regulatory principles and/or codes of conduct of these organisations. You can also opt out of our processing of your data by using the opt-out tools and consumer choice mechanisms provided by the EDAA here.

Our technology is configured to detect and honor the Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal. We treat this signal as a valid request to opt-out of the sale or sharing of personal information for the device or browser from which the signal originates, in accordance with applicable state laws.

Mobile Apps Most mobile devices provide device-level opt out by activating the "Limit Ad Tracking/App Tracking" (for iOS devices) or "Opt out of Ads Personalization" (for Android devices) option in your device"s settings. If you use more than one mobile device, you will need to change the settings on each device.

Smart/Connected TVs You can opt out of our data collection from CTVs by visiting the NAI CTV opt-out page. This explains how users can activate privacy features in many common TV and OTT environments.

L. Your Legal Rights

You have several rights regarding our processing of your personal data, including:

  • the right to request confirmation as to whether or not we are processing personal data concerning you, and, where that is the case, access to the personal data that we hold concerning you together with information about the nature, processing, and disclosure of your personal data;
  • the right to request that we correct inaccurate or update incomplete personal data concerning you;
  • the right to object to our processing of your personal data, in particular for processing carried out on the basis of our legitimate interest(s). If you object to our processing your personal data, we will cease processing it for such purposes;
  • the right to withdraw consent that you have given us to process your personal data, where applicable (note that such a withdrawal of consent will not affect processing that has already occurred);
  • the right to request that certain data about you be erased (note that this right is not absolute);
  • the right to propose restrictions on our processing of your personal data (e.g., if we have no legal right to keep using it); and
  • the right to have certain personal data transferred to another controller, in a structured, commonly-used, and machine-readable format (to the extent applicable).

You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), details of which can be found here.

If you are interested in exercising any of the rights described above, please submit a request here.

If you have questions about this Privacy Notice, please contact our Data Protection Officer by emailing privacy.department@nielsen.com or via postal mail to the address provided at the beginning of this notice. Please mark it for the attention of the Data Protection Officer.

M. Changes to Privacy Notice

We will update this Privacy Notice as required (e.g., changing business or personal data processing practices, technology, or legal requirements). When we make changes to this Privacy Notice, we will amend the "Last updated" date at the top of this page. We encourage users to visit this page periodically to review any updates and remain informed about how we are processing and protecting personal data.

Information for Data Subjects

Nielsen Media Research Limited (NMRL) obtains and processes personal data to provide its Nielsen Marketing Cloud (NMC) services to clients. Not all of this data is collected directly from individuals. You can learn more about this processing activity in our Article 14 Privacy Notice which is intended to meet the requirements of (UK) GDPR Article 14.5(b).  This notice includes information about the categories of personal data obtained, the purposes for which it’s obtained and how it’s shared.  You will also find information on data subject rights under the (UK) GDPR and how to exercise them.

Privacy Preference Center

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences, or your device, and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect. The information does not usually identify you directly, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to learn more and change our default settings. Blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.
More information

Manage Consent Preferences

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms.    You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site.    All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages.    If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites.    They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Social Media Cookies

These cookies are set by a range of social media services that we have added to the site to enable you to share our content with your friends and networks. They are capable of tracking your browser across other sites and building up a profile of your interests. This may impact the content and messages you see on other websites you visit.    If you do not allow these cookies you may not be able to use or see these sharing tools.
